samples.summary: Overlay guard disarms while the overlay is still mounted (exit animation), so a repeated/held Esc navigates out from behind a closing dialog
samples.evidence: Every branch of OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR requires data-state="open". Radix flips content to data-state="closed" on the dismissing Esc but keeps it mounted through the exit animation (ui/dialog + ui/sheet both carry data-[state=closed]:animate-out, i.e. Presence-held exit). Keyboard auto-repeat (or a fast second Esc) therefore produces a keydown while the ShareDialog/Sheet is still visibly on screen but already "closed": hasOpenOverlay() returns false and `onClose()` fires, navigating the user off /f/:id behind the closing overlay — exactly the failure mode the guard was added to prevent. The comment on lines 33-36 states this disarming is deliberate, but it reopens the hole for the repeat case.

samples.summary: useDocumentsPath returns "/documents" while the workspaces query is still in flight, so the back button / Esc / not-found redirect can land on the wrong list
samples.evidence: `const { data: workspaces = [] }` means during the first render(s) after a cold load of /f/:id (direct hit or refresh, no cached ["workspaces"]) the hook returns "/documents" rather than `/w/<slug>`. ImageFileLayout's `close` (file-detail.tsx:131-134) and FileShell's not-found redirect (file-shell.tsx:64-69) both consume that value synchronously, so a back-button click or Esc pressed in that window sends the user to the global documents list instead of the document's workspace. The hook has no loading/pending distinction for callers to wait on.

samples.summary: Not-found redirect effect can re-fire and toast twice when documentsPath changes after the workspaces query resolves
samples.evidence: The effect depends on `documentsPath`, which changes from "/documents" to "/w/<slug>" when the workspaces query resolves. If the component is still mounted at that point while `isDocumentError` remains true, `toast.error("Document not found")` fires a second time and a second navigate(..., {replace:true}) runs. (Same shape as the pre-change `fallbackSlug` dependency, so not a regression, but the diff carries it forward.)

samples.summary: hasOpenOverlay() only recognises Radix layers with role=dialog/alertdialog/menu/listbox or popper-hosted content; any other Esc-dismissable layer bypasses the guard
samples.evidence: OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR (image-viewer.tsx:22-38) enumerates specific Radix markup. Any Esc-dismissable overlay that is neither one of those roles nor a direct child of [data-radix-popper-content-wrapper] — e.g. a hand-rolled overlay closing on Escape, or a future non-popper Radix content wrapped in an extra div — will not be detected, and Esc will both dismiss it and navigate the viewer away. Nothing on the current image page appears to hit this (share dialog = Radix Dialog, mobile sidebar = Radix Sheet/Dialog, bell = Radix Popover in a popper wrapper), so confidence is low, but the guard is written as a global heuristic with no fallback.

samples.summary: Back/Esc pushes a new history entry to the workspace root, dropping the folder the image was opened from
samples.evidence: `navigate(documentsPath)` (no `replace`) always targets `/w/<slug>`, the workspace root list. A user who opened the image from a nested folder is returned to the root list, and the pushed entry means browser Back re-enters the viewer where Esc can be pressed again. FileShell's own not-found path uses `{ replace: true }`, so the two exits behave inconsistently.

samples.summary: With placeholderData: keepPreviousData, the not-found redirect can resolve the previous document's workspace
samples.evidence: `documentData` is kept from the previously viewed document (line 44) while the new documentId's fetch fails, so `useDocumentsPath(documentData?.workspaceId)` resolves the *previous* document's workspace and redirects there rather than to the requested document's (unknown) workspace or the fallback. Behaviour is unchanged from the pre-diff `workspaceSlug ?? workspaces[0]?.slug`, but the extracted hook now hides it.
